text:
lee: security researcher reported a Pastebin posting containing what looks like a Datadog API key (starts with "ddog_api_key_"). Possibly copied from an old playbook. Treat as compromised and rotate.

nina: thanks. repo/playbook?

lee: playbook: infra/runbooks/incident-monitoring.md (public fork). Key shown: ddog_api_key_example123. Affects monitoring write keys for staging cluster only, per naming.

samir: I'll rotate the key and update secrets. Plan: 1) revoke old API key in Datadog 2) create new key 3) update Vault path secret/monitoring/datadog-staging 4) restart metric forwarder. ETA 20m.

ops-bot: action started: creating maintenance window for staging metric ingestion. Blocking inbound metric posts that use old key.

nina: add audit: check for any metric or log writes from unknown IPs in last 48h and search for push events using that key across webhook history.

samir: revoked old key -> datadog_revocation_id: dd-revoke-2026-11-03-02. Wrote new key to Vault: secret/monitoring/datadog-staging. Restarted forwarder: rollout succeeded.

sec-bot: reminder: rotate any downstream integrations that may have cached the key (alerting webhooks, lambda forwarders).

lee: notifying oncall and product that staging alerts may be delayed for ~10m. Also filing INC-2026-512 for tracking.

nina: audit shows 0 suspicious writes to prod metrics. Only staging ingestion seen from our CI egress IPs. Good to close after partner confirmation.

lee: closing thread as actioned. Follow-up: add pre-commit CI secret scan and update runbook to avoid raw keys in examples.
